2. It appears that the rule was not correctly drawn up. This should be an application for condonation of delay of 599 days in filing F.A.T. No.602 of 2002. We have perused the memorandum of appeal and the decree of the trial court and it appears that after the decree was passed in the suit, the defendant as appellant preferred F.A.T. No.602 of 2002 which was delayed by 599 days and for condonation of the said delay this application was filed and rule was issued. We shall accordingly treat the rule as one for condonation of delay of 599 days in filing the F.A.T. No.602 of 2002. 

 5. The rule was issued only on the plaintiff-respondent. In any view, we have heard the learned Advocates and perused the statements made in the application for condonation of delay and also the supplementary affidavit. The impugned judgment and decree was passed on 26.11.2000 and decree was signed on 30.11.2000 by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) and Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.107 of 2000 who decreed the suit. The present petitioner, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka, who was a contesting defendant in the suit applied for the certified copy on 19.6.2002, about 2 years after the impugned decree and the certified copy was made ready and delivered on 29.6.2002 and this was informed to the petitioner on 25.7.2002. Thereafter this F.A.T No.602 of 2002 was filed on 3.9.2002. When the memorandum of appeal was presented to the stamp reporter on 4.9.2002, it was found that there was a delay of 599 days in filing the appeal. Thereafter this rule for condonation of delay was issued on 24.11.1992. On a perusal of the application for condonation of delay we do not find any explanation as regards delay of 599 days in filing the appeal. In Paragraph No.4 it is stated that the suit was decreed on 26.11.2000 (decree signed on 30.11.2000) and the conducting Advocate Mr. A.S.M. Moslemuddin Ahmed made application on 19.6.2002 for obtaining certified copy of the judgment and decree which was made ready and delivered on 29.6.2002. It appears that there is absolutely no explanation from 30.11.2000, the date when the decree was of signed till 19.6.2002 the date for filing the application for certified copy. In paragraph No.3 of the application for condonation of delay. it is stated that the petitioner requested the Legal Adviser, vested property and Senior Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Land vide Memo No.224(e)(m) vested property/2002 dated 17.8.2002 for filing appeal and the Legal Adviser, vested property received the file on 25.8.2002 and there was correspondence with Secretary, Ministry of Land vide Memo No.4980(3093) dated 25.8.2002 for providing with law costs for filing the appeal and there was a delay of 599 days in filing the appeal before this court. It, therefore, appears that there is absolutely no explanation for obtaining the certified copy after about 2 years after the suit was decreed. Subsequently the matter appeared in the list for hearing on 3.8.2006 when another Division Bench allowed the opposite party to file a reply to the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner. In the said supplementary affidavit attempt has been made to explain the delay in filing the application for certified copy, which is an after-thought. 

 6. We have perused the statements made in the supplementary affidavit which was swoi n on 2.8.2006 with an attempt to explain the delay. The deponent is the Assistant Secretary, Section 9, ministry of Land. Dhaka who was not competent to explain the delay of about 2 years in obtaining the certified copy of the impugned judgment and decree by the conducting Advocate or his law clerk. The statement made in the supplementary affidavit appears to be an attempt to fill up the lacuna in the application for condonation of delay and we are not inclined to accept such explanation. The opposite party (plaintiff) obtained the decree in 2002 and should not be deprived of the fruit of the decree in the absence of cogent and satisfactory explanation for the delay in obtaining the certified copy of the impugned judgment and decree. A vested right accrued in favour of the plaintiff which can not he any taken away on the basis of the application for condonation of delay which does not 'contain each days delay. The learned Advocate for the petitioner Mr. Rahiul Alam Chowdhury does not appear to support the rule.
